lines.text: Hold a button, and the robot drives itself to a spot on the field.
Every meter so far, a person drove. Now the robot uses its own pose.
The goal is a pose too: three meters, two meters, facing the other way.
The command is the same loop you already know. Start, run every loop, check if it's done, and stop on the way out.
Three controllers run at once: one for X, one for Y, and one for heading. Each one turns its error into a speed.
Heading needs one extra line. Otherwise, turning from a hundred seventy nine degrees to minus a hundred seventy nine goes the long way around.
Three meters out, with a gain of ten, it asks for thirty meters per second. The robot can't do that, so it runs flat out.
Try it. Drag the goal somewhere else, and hold the button.
Close to the goal, the error is small, so the speed is small, and it creeps up short. That's the falls short shape from tuning.
Let go, and the command ends with a zero speed request. Sending idle instead would leave every wheel on its last speed.
Speed from distance gets you there, badly. Next, plan the trip.
